result.summary: This PR fixes the fallback (non-posix_fallocate) implementation of AllocateFileRange, which previously unconditionally zero-filled the requested byte range even when it overlapped existing file contents, clobbering block data during -reindex on platforms lacking posix_fallocate (BSDs, OmniOS, OpenIndiana). It changes the fallback to only zero-fill bytes beyond the current end of file. It also updates the Windows path to check the current file size and only extend the file when the requested range exceeds it, rather than unconditionally truncating/extending, following work from a related closed PR (#33228).
result.problem: On systems without posix_fallocate, AllocateFileRange's fallback path zero-fills the whole requested range regardless of existing content, so running -reindex overwrites blk*.dat with zeros before the reindex scan reads them, leaving only the genesis block after supposedly successful reindexing. This affects users running Bitcoin Core on *BSD, OmniOS, and OpenIndiana, per issue #33128.

open_concerns: Author is considering (not yet implementing) making AllocateFileRange strictly append-only, pending input from another contributor (sedited) referenced from a related PR discussion; this is exploratory and not blocking the current fix.

result.card: This PR fixes a data-corruption bug in the fallback AllocateFileRange implementation used on platforms without posix_fallocate (BSDs, OmniOS, OpenIndiana), where -reindex would zero-fill and destroy existing block data, silently leaving only the genesis block after reindexing. It also hardens the Windows path to avoid unconditional file truncation/extension. The linked open issue #33128 corroborates real user impact: '-reindex was broken on platforms using the fallback implementation.' Review is currently Ready, with only minor style nits raised by one contributor reviewer (thomasbuilds), all addressed via force-pushes; no maintainer has weighed in yet. The author is also considering, but has not implemented, a further scope change toward append-only semantics pending outside input. This PR supersedes two prior closed attempts at the same fix (#33164, #33228).
